title: `merge <pr> --ready` stops at a time limit and prints which step or debt command it waits on, instead of hanging silently
why: Finding (coordinator 13:46 CST Nov 14, from runner 10's logs ready3400.log and ready3400b.log; triage read none): `merge 3400 --ready` hung twice, 36 min and 11 min, after `ste-lint: PASS`. A python3 chain with a 600 s-old `sleep` child sat under it; no output, no timeout. Other PRs get the next line within 3 s. Debt candidate named by runner 10: the ready step has no timeout and prints nothing while a step waits, so a hang reads as slowness. Cost: 47 min of the runner's turn, n=1 PR, 2 runs. Cause on #3400 unknown; its lane is reproducing the single step now and was told not to run --ready. Not an owner question yet. Kin: merge-tool-beats-every-phase (a timed progress line per phase; its phase beat merged in #3404), stall-watch-ends-quiet-jobs, ready-checks-job-qualified-steps. First act of a lane: read what runs after `ste-lint` in `--ready`, reproduce the hang, then red then green: a `--ready` step that waits longer than its limit stops and names the step, and every step prints a line within a stated time. Check change: if a verdict moves, round 3 applies. REPRO 13:47 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 13:49): the #3400 lane cannot reproduce the hang on its head; runner 10 is asked for one more background rerun with a process snapshot at the stall. Cause still unknown. CAUSE NARROWED 13:57 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 14:00, runner 10's fifth run, process probe at a 65 s stall, its log ready3400e.log; triage read none): the stuck process is the debt-close lint, not the STE lint. The poller python3 (age 69 s) runs with cwd /tmp/debt-retire-<random>/tree; its parent runs in the claude-settings checkout and reads its pipes. #3405, #3412 and #3413 passed the same ready step, so it is PR-specific: one of #3400's six debt files (docs/debts/red-run-*.md and notes.md) may have a retire command that waits in a bare temp tree (unproven; the lane is testing it). Two defects whichever file it is: (1) the ready step has no timeout and prints no row while a debt command runs, so a stall reads as slowness (cost: 5 runs, about 90 min of runner 10 time, n=1 PR); (2) the lane's earlier guess (a step child holding ci-job's pipe, bin/ci-job:513-519) is ruled out for this case. Not an owner question.
